feature_description: Handles user login, session management, and access control. Users authenticate via username/password or LDAP. Successful authentication creates a server-side session with role-based permissions. Sessions expire after 30 minutes of inactivity or 8 hours absolute. Failed login attempts are tracked and accounts lock after 5 consecutive failures.

business_rules.summary: Account locks after 5 consecutive failed login attempts
business_rules.details: Each failed login increments a counter on the user record. When the counter reaches 5, the account status is set to LOCKED and all subsequent login attempts are rejected regardless of correct credentials. The counter resets to 0 on successful login. Locked accounts require admin intervention to unlock — there is no automatic unlock timer.
business_rules.pseudocode:
ON failed_login(user):
  user.failed_attempts = user.failed_attempts + 1
  IF user.failed_attempts >= 5 THEN
    user.status = LOCKED
  SAVE user

ON login_attempt(user):
  IF user.status == LOCKED THEN
    REJECT "Account is locked. Contact administrator."

behavioral_contracts: GIVEN a user with 4 failed attempts WHEN login fails THEN account status is set to LOCKED
GIVEN a locked account WHEN login attempted with correct password THEN login is rejected
GIVEN a user with 0 failed attempts WHEN login fails 4 times THEN account remains ACTIVE
edge_cases: Concurrent login attempts reaching threshold simultaneously
User already locked receives additional failed attempts

business_rules.summary: Failed login counter resets on successful authentication
business_rules.details: On successful password verification, the failed_attempts field is set to 0 and last_login timestamp is updated. This happens before session creation, so a user who was at 4 failed attempts and then logs in successfully starts fresh.
business_rules.pseudocode:
ON successful_login(user):
  user.failed_attempts = 0
  user.last_login = NOW()
  SAVE user

behavioral_contracts: GIVEN a user with 4 failed attempts WHEN login succeeds THEN failed_attempts is 0
GIVEN a successful login WHEN checking last_login THEN timestamp is updated to current time
edge_cases: Reset during concurrent failed attempt from another session
Database failure during reset (partial write: counter reset but last_login not updated)

business_rules.summary: Sessions expire after 30 minutes idle or 8 hours absolute
business_rules.details: Two independent expiry checks: (1) idle timeout — if last_activity is more than 30 minutes ago, session is invalid; (2) absolute timeout — if session_created is more than 8 hours ago, session is invalid regardless of activity. Both are checked on every authenticated request via the SessionFilter.
business_rules.pseudocode:
FUNCTION is_session_valid(session):
  IF (now - session.last_activity) > 30 MINUTES THEN
    RETURN false  // idle timeout
  IF (now - session.created_at) > 8 HOURS THEN
    RETURN false  // absolute timeout
  RETURN true

test_oracle.location: No tests found for SessionFilter timeout logic
behavioral_contracts: GIVEN a session idle for 31 minutes WHEN request arrives THEN session is invalid
GIVEN a session idle for 29 minutes WHEN request arrives THEN session is valid
GIVEN a session created 8 hours 1 second ago WHEN request arrives THEN session is invalid regardless of activity

components.name: AuthController
components.description: REST endpoint for authentication operations. Handles login requests and delegates to LoginService.

functions.name: login
functions.description: Accept login credentials and return session token on success.

components.name: LoginService
components.description: Core authentication logic. Handles account lockout, auth source routing, and credential verification.

functions.name: authenticate
functions.description: Main entry point: verify credentials, handle lockout, route to correct auth provider.

components.name: SessionManager
components.description: Manages server-side sessions. Creates sessions with role-resolved permissions and handles session lookup/invalidation.

functions.name: createSession
functions.description: Create a new session with fully resolved permissions from user's roles.

functions.name: getSession
functions.description: Look up a session by token.

components.name: SessionFilter
components.description: HTTP filter that validates session tokens on every authenticated request. Enforces idle and absolute timeouts.

functions.name: doFilter
functions.description: Intercept requests, validate session, enforce timeout rules.

control_flows.summary: User login with lockout and auth routing

steps.action: Validate request body contains username and password
steps.decision: If request body missing required fields, return 400 Bad Request.

steps.action: Look up user by username in the database
steps.decision: If user not found, return authentication failure.
If user.failed_attempts >= 5, reject login with 'Account locked' message.
If user.auth_source == 'LDAP', use LDAP bind. Otherwise, use bcrypt compare.

steps.action: On success: reset counter and create session
steps.decision: Set failed_attempts to 0, update last_login, create session with resolved permissions.
Return 200 with session token and user profile.

control_flows.migration_impact: No direct changes. Login flow logic remains unchanged during migration.

steps.action: Extract session token from Authorization header
steps.decision: If no Authorization header present, return 401 Unauthorized.

steps.action: Look up session in session store
steps.decision: If session not found, return 401 Unauthorized.
If idle > 30 min or absolute > 8 hours, invalidate session and return 401.
Set session.last_activity to now, attach user context, proceed with filter chain.

control_flows.migration_impact: Session storage will move from in-memory to distributed cache. Session validation must handle cache misses and replica lag.

entities.name: User
entities.description: Core user account representing a person who can authenticate. Stores credentials, authentication state (failed attempts, lockout), and auth source routing.

attributes.name: username
attributes.description: Login identifier, unique across the system

attributes.name: password_hash
attributes.description: Bcrypt-hashed password. NULL for LDAP-only users.

attributes.name: status
attributes.description: Account status: ACTIVE, LOCKED, or DISABLED

attributes.name: failed_attempts
attributes.description: Consecutive failed login count. Resets on success, locks at 5.

attributes.name: last_login
attributes.description: When the user last successfully authenticated

entities.name: Session
entities.description: Server-side session object holding authenticated user context. Contains resolved permissions from all user roles. Used for authorization checks on every request.

attributes.name: token
attributes.description: Unique session identifier sent to client

attributes.name: permissions
attributes.description: Flattened set of permission strings from all user roles

attributes.name: createdAt
attributes.description: When this session was created (for absolute timeout)

internal.description: AuthController delegates authentication logic to LoginService.
LoginService calls SessionManager.createSession() after successful authentication.
SessionFilter uses SessionManager.getSession() for session lookup on every request.

external.name: Corporate LDAP Directory
external.description: Used for authenticating LDAP-sourced users via bind operation. No fallback if unreachable.

external.name: PostgreSQL Database
external.description: Stores user accounts, roles, and permissions. Used for credential verification and session permission resolution.
